exposure: standard surgical technique laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterectomy (LAVH)
cohort: 101 patients undergoing hysterectomy at the Clinic of Gynaecology, Obstetrics and Gynaecological Oncology at the Pius Hospital, University Hospital for Gynaecology in Oldenburg
finding: There were no significant differences between LACH and LAVH regarding outcome parameters, even when considering risk factors like large uterus size, vaginal nulliparity, or prior caesarean section.
mod_finding: Patients with prior caesarean sections in both LACH and LAVH groups showed significant differences in the number of leukocytes on the 2nd postoperative day.
